sources.entry: Postfix - Fast, easy to administer, and secure Sendmail replacement. IPL-1.0 C/deb

summary.name: Postfix
summary.one_liner: Postfix is a fast, easy-to-administer, and secure mail transfer agent (MTA) and Sendmail replacement, originally written by Wietse Venema.
use_cases: Replacing Sendmail on a UNIX-like system
Relaying SMTP mail on Linux servers
summary.what_it_does: Postfix is a mail server originally developed by Wietse Venema at IBM research as an alternative to Sendmail. The page describes it as aiming to be fast, easy to administer, and secure, with a Sendmail-like outward flavor but a completely different internal design. The project distributes source code that can be built on UNIX-like systems including AIX, BSD, HP-UX, Linux, MacOS X, and Solaris. Vendors also ship ready-to-run builds that may differ slightly from the source described on the site.
notable: Sendmail-compatible in outward flavor but internally different
Wietse Venema maintains it after eight years at Google
Distributed as source code and by OS and appliance vendors
Listed under IPL-1.0 license in awesome-selfhosted
caveats: Vendor-packaged versions may differ slightly from the software described on the website
Page covers source distribution only; no installation or configuration details given
